sentence: This project studies how cytokines secreted by myeloproliferative neoplasm cells help separate clones grow and lead to acute myeloid leukemia.
This project sets up wastewater genomic monitoring to detect Neisseria gonorrhoeae and antimicrobial resistance mutations early.
This project studies how everyday exposures to violence and belonging in an area affect safety, physiological stress, mental health and substance use in adolescents.
This project offers shared support for studying how environmental exposures, including metals, organic solvents and airborne particulate matter, affect human health.
This project uses chemical biology methods to study glycosylated molecules and looks for genes that regulate their production.
This project tests whether cognitive performance in older breast cancer survivors stays stable or declines more than in individuals without a cancer history.
This project builds a rapid platform that uses an under-oil open microfluidic system to identify infecting organisms and test antimicrobial susceptibility.
This project tests a drug combined with gene therapy as a treatment for a children's disease called pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency.
This project provides biostatistical and bioinformatics expertise so investigators can manage, analyze and share data in a reliable and reproducible way.
This project looks for drug targets in the sexual cycle of the fungi that cause Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in persons with HIV.
This project tries to find out what conditions in the developing embryo produce hematopoietic stem cells so they can be made in vitro.
This project provides imaging tools and targeted radiation for cancer studies in animal models, with standard methods that make results reproducible.
This project tests whether directly reprogramming somatic cells into lymphatic endothelial cells can treat lymphedema in animal models.
This project uses cryo-electron microscopy and structural mass spectrometry to study how proteins merge two membranes into one in enveloped viruses.
This project compares brain cells from individuals with autism spectrum disorder and unaffected controls to find differing patterns of gene expression.
This project provides DNA-based assays that check how genome editing affects the target site and off-target regions of the genome.
This project studies vesicle fusion, where two lipid bilayers merge into one, and how imbalances in it are linked to metabolic disorders.
This project supports vision research on the eye and visual system, from basic mechanisms of vision to therapies for people with vision disorders.
This project studies how changes in glycan sulfation in perineuronal nets link to neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds an animal model to study the genetic, molecular and neural circuit factors behind social attachment deficits in frontotemporal dementia.
